purpose: Show agencies how white-label work with Alliance AI Partners runs: we build under the agency’s brand, the client relationship stays theirs, embedded developers when they need more hands, a fixed quote first and published starting prices, the four steps, and confidentiality terms to confirm. images.source: Editorial illustration on a soft Daylight sky at daybreak. A large faceted paper kite, folded from flat planes in Partner Navy and slate blue, flies out in front, trailing a long satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan. A small flock of faceted paper swallows flies close behind the kite in a tight, orderly formation, following the ribbon: one shape leads and a capable team works behind it. The kite is plain, with no marks, symbols or letters. A low band of flat faceted paper hills in pale blue-grey runs along the bottom edge. Keep the upper left quarter calm and empty. Near-square, about 1:1, safe to crop to 4:5. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. Nature built from satin ribbon and flat paper facets. Light from the upper left, soft navy-tinted shadows falling down and to the right. No text or letters, no people, no hands, no robots, no brains, no circuit boards, no sparkles, no glow, no purple or pink, no regional or cultural motifs, no real places or landmarks.

notes: Promises come from the Brand DNA only: the white-label line is the Brand DNA's service entry ('We deliver AI projects under your agency's brand, so you can offer AI without hiring'), 'from planning to launch' is its Agency services entry, the embedded-developer lead is its Embedded developers entry, the price promises are verbatim from 'Our honest pricing promise' (confirm each is true before launch), and the rest come from its values and 'Questions buyers will ask'. 'The client relationship stays yours' follows from the white-label line and was asked for in the brief for this page: confirm it before launch. NDA and confidentiality terms are placeholders. The page says 'clients' for the agency's own customers, the word agencies use; 'partners' still means the agencies. The contact links use a new ?service=white-label value, which the contact form needs to accept. No figures on the page, so no sources. Header marks no nav item. One Primary in the hero and one in the closing band. Review 2026-11-03: the White-label head and its large card no longer repeat the hero (title, lead and “Your brand on the work”); full name in the Embedded developers lead; line breaks keep single words off the last line of three headings. Still for the owner: whether the client relationship stays with the agency, and a direct yes or no to “Will my clients know you’re involved?”. Lead image pass 2026-11-03: section-specific images replace backgrounds that repeated across pages.
